summary: Round 12 did everything in direction 26a's closing order, then ran its one arm: the round-12 tree against round-11/arm-final11 on all 15 sweep-9 hand-overs to winter. All four of direction 26's bars are met. Median protein intake / need went 0.329 -> 0.482 (bar 0.45). Brood hygiene deaths went 60 -> 9 (bar 31). Viable went 13 -> 14, with the kitchen door at 3 of 3 (we #2 went from 6 to 13 workers and is now viable). Every colony that met R27's winter carbohydrate in the base still meets it. Workers at winter 243 -> 266 (10 better, 4 worse), trip success 51.6 % -> 62.2 %, tend time 518 -> 249 worker game days, forage time 532 -> 643. One bar is not met: the behaviours system on kd #1 fell from 0.728 to 0.351 ms a tick, against a bar of 0.30. Direction 26a item 3's switch-off probe found that no single R38 item caused the hygiene rise. The mechanism was a defect in the flood hold: a hauler was held outside for any water at all on the brood-chamber floor (0.01-0.17 BU). That is fixed together with the ruled hold limit, the haul cap and nurses carrying waste. The 26.2 trace found no defect in the forage choice; the numbers are written down for the integrator's ruling. Everything is recorded in the ledger under "## Round 12" (progress log plus "### Round 12 results"). Evidence is in /home/user/foundress/test-output/colony-life/round-12/.
causesRanked: 1. Protein not taken: median P intake 0.329 (arm) / 0.353 (sweep 11). The arm delivered 155 P against a larval demand of 326 P. Worker time went to tend (518 worker game days in the arm, 15-35 % of task time in colonies that had their winter carbohydrate by day 4-8) and to scouting that found nothing (252 of 299 scout trips in sweep 11). Fixes: R39, 26a.2, 26.3, 26a.1.

2. Brood hygiene: 60 deaths in the arm, 56 in sweep 11, the largest brood loss. On cpv #2 (6 gd), switching off R38 item 1, 2 or 4 changed the trajectory and removed the burst: 0-6 dirty hours, 0 deaths, against 71 hours and 14 deaths with all items on; items 3+5 changed nothing. The mechanism: the colony's one hauler was held outside by the flood hold (65 holds in 6 gd, all for a brood-chamber floor with 0.01-0.17 BU of water, 58 of 71 dirty hours), while a first pupation left a burst of meconium. Fixed as D32.

3. Per-tick cost: R38 item 5's smell check made ecology/sources/lookup.ts rebuild its whole grid on nearly every tick. Behaviours went from 0.25 to 0.70 ms a tick. Fixed in 26a.0 (0.728 -> 0.351 on kd #1).
4. Scout floor order (minor): a colony of 6 sent 2 scouts ahead of forage. Fixed in 26.3.

Protein fell in some colonies: cpv #3 0.31 -> 0.25, kd #3 0.67 -> 0.55, pp #1 0.56 -> 0.48. The 26.2 trace points to protein that is not known (discovery), plus the value form where both nutrients are known, which is for the integrator to rule.

gddDeviations: R38b (GDD 02 §6.2-6.3): only the scout floor is served ahead of forage. The floor has two levels: the full floor while nothing of the nutrient is known, and max(1, ceil(0.1 N)) once a live source is known but the colony is still short. Scouts report food they smell in every phase except explore and investigate.

R39 (GDD 02 §6.2): tend demand = min(sum of slots, max(keep, ceil(1.25 x wantC / carbohydrate one tender brings a gd))). wantC leaves out what known non-herd sources and marked herds supply. The keep is 1 tender a herd, more for herds over 200 aphids so that tend stays above RIVAL_TEND_GUARD.

D32 (GDD 03 §11.3, GDD 02 §6.2, §10.4): the surface hold needs water at least FLEE_WATER_DEPTH_BU deep and never lasts longer than FLEE_HOLD_MAX_GD 0.1. While brood lies among waste the haul cap is 0.4 N, and a nurse with no job carries waste out of a brood chamber that is over tolerance.
The R38 row's pointers were updated: nutrientMissing and withScoutsFirst were removed.
notesForIntegrator: All four bars of direction 26 item 5 are met. Not met: 26a.0's behaviours bar on kd #1 (0.351 against 0.30). The identity run with the grid fix alone read 0.341.

26a.3: no single R38 item raised hygiene. Switching off any of items 1, 2 or 4 removed cpv #2's burst only because it changed the trajectory. The mechanism is the flood hold: walkingIntoWater held an ant for water > 0, while an ant inside only flees at 0.15 BU. I read 'the way to her destination passes a flooded cell' as the destination floor, because all 65 holds were there; no path test was built.

26.2 is a stop-and-write-numbers case. In the 2 gd traced on cpv #3 there was no known protein when the colony took its carbohydrate trips. The one case with both nutrients known shows the value form: U = value / trip seconds favours an 8 BU flower 4.9x over a 154 BU carcass, although the protein load is worth 1.7x per trip.

26.1: the forage cap is not what holds the freed workers (nobody is idle). The prospective part of the forage demand is filled last (R35 point 5), so on days 0-1 the freed tenders go to other tasks first.

R39 uses the double-count subtraction: the forage demand already asks foragers for the carbohydrate that known non-herd sources give, so that carbohydrate is left out of the tenders' want. TEND_HEADROOM was not tuned.

Two test changes: the tendHerd.test fixture's colony now starts with C 0.5 instead of 30, because under R39 a colony with its carbohydrate covered keeps 1 tender a herd (tend 0.49); the test checks tending mechanics. The scoutsFirst.verify call now passes the floor number instead of a flag.
